name: g9-Battle-Scene
description: Fork of g2-Battle-Scene, tightly coupled to g9-battle-engine -- unlike that mod (a standalone library, left untouched), this one owns no combat rules of its own at all. Turn resolution calls mod.exports.resolveTurnActions on g9-battle-engine (STAB/Tera/Protect/damage/accuracy/sub-effects all live there, per the standing 'combat logic lives in g9-battle-engine only' rule), while EXP/catch call the real native Gen 2 primitives (Battle:awardExperience, src/battle/gen2/Catching.lua) directly rather than a hand-ported copy. Same named battle-layout index (layouts/<name>.lua presets) and rendering as g2-Battle-Scene; a calling mod picks a preset by name and supplies the battler roster via mod.exports.pushLayoutBattle. All presets share ONE standardized 16:9 field geometry: a 960x540 canvas -- the file's 320x180 design field drawn at x3 (see DS), so it is a clean sub-multiple of every standard display (x1 = 960x540, x2 = 1920x1080, x4 = 4K, x8 = 8K) and the canvas now FILLS the real window at the exact fractional fit ratio (v1.8.2) instead of integer-letterboxing, so the bottom message/menu band's own bottom frame lands ON the screen's bottom edge at every window size and the field is as tall as the display allows; on an exact 960x540 multiple that scale is still a whole number, so the ratio is respected and nothing is distorted, and on any other size it fills the limiting dimension with minimal bars on the other; the sprite pack bakes its natural-size art at the canvas resolution and it is blitted 1:1, so species art reaches the screen at its real resolution rather than being baked small and magnified -- an eight-column sprite grid whose centre-to-centre pitch IS the readout's own pitch -- 56.4px drawn width + a 2px gap, i.e. COL_W, defined off HUD_W -- so a side's columns and its row of readouts share one spacing and every readout stands dead over its own mon (a very wide sprite can still overhang the field's own left/right edge) -- which still draw over the field, so nothing is hidden behind them; each battler now carries its OWN readout box, over its own slot: box i belongs to battler i and is centred on that battler's own slot centre-x (the point its sprite is centred on), so moving a sprite moves its readout with it -- the readouts used to be one STACKED column per team at a single x, and are now split one-per-slot -- with a side's boxes laid out in a single row, one box per slot on the mon's own centre-x (the grid's pitch is the readout's own, so no spreading is needed; spreadBoxCentres survives only as the safety net for an over-full row that really does overlap) and every box on a side kept at the SAME height -- one head line per side, not one per mon -- so the row reads level, each box's bottom edge sitting on that shared line and so ON the head of its pokemon, the head line being 70% of each SPRITE'S OWN drawn height above its own feet, averaged over the sprites that side actually has on the field (measured per sprite from what was really drawn, not from a shared slot/row line) -- the native HUD tiles' shade 0 dropped out -- with the box frame and its white interior fill both gone, so each readout is the cart's native assets alone (name, level, gender, HP bar, numeric and exp bar) floating over its pokemon with no rectangle drawn around them, and the pokemon reads through it), and two DISJOINT ground lines so the two teams can never share a y range. The ally team fills the grid RIGHTWARD from a1 (cols 1..4) and the enemy team fills it LEFTWARD from e6 (cols 2..6), so each side leaves its OUTER columns empty when it is under strength -- a lone ally stands at a1 and a lone enemy at e6. The ally half of the grid is anchored at a1 = 35px (ALLY_LEFT_X), the exact spot the old +50px-shifted grid gave the lead ally, so a lone ally does not move; the enemy half is anchored at e6 = 276.8px so the five-mon horde's 290px readout row keeps the same margin at each end of the 320px canvas. The player trainer's intro back-pic (drawn into the first ally's slot) rides along with the ally anchor. A boss enemy always takes column e5 (col 5); a horde's lone ally takes a2 (col 2). A preset may field up to five enemies and four allies. A slot is an ANCHOR -- its column's centre-x and its side's ground line -- never a box the art is folded into: every sprite is drawn at its SIDE's own scale -- SPRITE_SCALE_FRONT for the enemy team (and the boss), SPRITE_SCALE_BACK for the ally team, two INDEPENDENT multipliers, both 1 by default -- x its own trimmed pixels at its FULL natural size -- there is NO picture-box cap: an oversized pack frame keeps every pixel (v1.8.1 removed the old 56px front / 48px back fold, which flattened a mon the moment it passed that size), so a Diglett stays small and a Koraidon stays as huge as its art, and no two species are forced to the same height or width; a side's scale simply multiplies every sheet on that side. A sprite is then drawn at its FULL natural size with NO fold of any kind (v1.8.2 removed the LAST cap, the field-headroom fold ABOVE each side's ground line -- 128px for an ally, 64px for an enemy -- which shrank any sheet taller than that band), so a species whose art stands taller than the field simply draws past the top of the scene and is cut by the screen edge rather than being shrunken; a wide species may reach past its own column (even under a HUD box), which is the point. A preset may set spriteScaleFront / spriteScaleBack (or the legacy single spriteScale, which sets both) to change either multiplier. The bossFight boss is drawn at SPRITE_SCALE x 1.6 (the +0.6, bosses only), CENTRED on e5 and anchored to the top of the field so it towers over the enemy half instead of standing down among the allies, and it draws at its full natural size like every other sheet -- NO fold -- so it may run off the top of the field rather than being shrunken. The 'singles' preset is the ordinary one-on-one wild-encounter field -- the one Sample-Battle-Scene routes its wild encounters to, so they use this scene instead of the native battle screen. Move animations are remapped to play from the ACTOR's real on-screen position (a non-uniform scale stretches vanilla's own baked travel to the real actor-target gap), and a SPREAD move (one that hits a whole side -- g9-battle-engine's exported isSpreadMove) is instead cast on the MIDDLE of the OPPOSING side's sprite area: an enemy's spread move centres over the player's team and a player's over the enemy's, so the animation washes over the side rather than snapping to one victim. A WILD-encounter mon (and only a wild one -- a trainer's mon is still thrown out of a pokeball) now appears IN PLACE at its final sprite position, fading from completely invisible to completely visible over one second (WILD_FADE_DURATION), instead of the old drop-in from the top of the screen. A trainer's send-out now pre-warms that mon's sheet during the pokeball's flight and draws NOTHING while it bakes, so the sprite never flashes its vanilla pic for its first frames. In the boss fight the boss alone now stands 40 screen px (of the 960x540 canvas) lower, so it sits clear of the field's top edge while keeping its size -- and its HUD readout and the pokeball's landing spot follow it down. In v1.8.3 the trainer intro pics are drawn in the cart's own colours: the player's back-pic and a trainer's class front-pic are 4-shade grayscale sheets, so each is remapped through its own TrainerPalettes row (Palettes.trainerColors + GbcPalette.with -- exactly the arm native's BattleState:drawPic uses), honouring a player.sprite swap for the back-pic and a classDef.trueColor flag for either, instead of being drawn raw, which had left both grey. In v1.8.4 the field's two sprite scales are set to 0.5 (SPRITE_SCALE_FRONT and SPRITE_SCALE_BACK, both halves), the stand-in trainer intro pic is 5 tiles (TRAINER_PIC_T), the bossfight boss's size ratio is 1.5 (BOSS_MUL, so a boss draws at SPRITE_SCALE_FRONT x 1.5) and the boss's own position nudge is -60 canvas px on y (BOSS_Y_SHIFT), replacing the previous 1/1 scales, 7-tile pic, 1.6 boss ratio and +40 y shift respectively. In v1.8.5 the mod runs on BOTH generations: a new generation backend (native.lua) detects the running generation at load and gives the scene a per-generation shim for the handful of engine surfaces it touches -- chosen so the Gen 2 path is unchanged by construction, since every symbol maps 1:1 onto the exact gen2 module or data.gen2* field it required before -- and the manifest's games list now admits gen1 alongside gen2. On Gen 1 the scene's combat authority is the GAME'S OWN Gen 1 engine: BattleState:performMove (accuracy, damage, effects, status, PP -- the real native executor, not a reimplementation) sequenced by the real src.battle.TurnOrder, because g9-battle-engine is a Gen 2 engine whose model cannot drive a Gen 1 BattleState; a future gen-1-capable engine mod can take over by exporting resolveTurnActionsForGen1(battle, acting), checked first. EXP uses the same pure src.pokemon.Growth + Experience.apply the native screen is built on, catch calls src.battle.Catching.attempt, and the readout reuses the pure HP-bar math (src.battle.gen2.HpBar) over Gen 1's own HudTiles.drawHPBar at the same 48px width. Stated Gen 1 gaps, not crashes: no move animations (Gen 1's AnimPlayer data shape is a different contract and is left unwired), no exp bar on the player readout (Gen 1 has no in-battle exp bar), trainer intro art draws raw (Gen 1's SGB colouring is a native-screen pipeline this scene does not reproduce), the BAG is a ball-only native ListMenu wired straight to the scene's own throwBall (Gen 1's native BagMenu throws through the native BattleState, not this scene's model), and switching goes through the native PartyMenu. In v1.8.6 those Gen 1 gaps are lifted whenever the build ALSO carries the Gen 2 asset tables (a Gen 1 boot that bundles Gold's data, or a content mod that merges a data.gen2* registry -- a stock Red/Blue/Yellow boot has none of them): the Gen 1 arm calls the whole Gen 2 asset set into Gen 1 -- it reads palette / menu-gfx / status / trainer / constants / anim data from the same data.gen2* fields the Gen 2 arm reads, builds the real Gen 2 battle HUD (so Gen 1 gets the cart's $60-$78 tiles and a real exp bar back), loads the Gen 2 move-animation engine (AnimRunner + BattleAnimView), colours trainer intro art through the Gen 2 palette rows (player back-pic off gen2MenuGfx.battleHud, class front-pic off gen2Trainers / menu-gfx, honouring trueColor), and uses authored Gen 2 status labels. The trigger is ASSET PRESENCE, detected off the live game data at load, not the generation switch: with no Gen 2 assets present none of those modules are even loaded and every Gen 1 path is exactly what it was. Species battle pics still cannot come from Gen 2 either way (data.gen2Sprites is overworld/icon sheets, not the data.pokemon[species] battle art the scene draws). Gold/Silver behaviour is preserved byte-for-byte. In v1.8.7 the Gen 1 boot no longer dies at load: the Gen 1 arm required src.battle.gen2.HpBar for its pure HP-bar maths, but the engine's cross-generation require gate (src/mods/Loader.lua's crossGenerationDenial) refuses every require("src.*.gen2.*") on a Gen 1 game, so the whole mod failed to load there (and every mod depending on it, e.g. Sample-Battle-Scene-G9, failed with it). That pure, require-free module is now vendored as this mod's own hp_bar.lua and loaded as a sibling by the Gen 1 arm; the Gen 2 arm still requires the real engine module and is unchanged. In v1.8.8 the Gen 1 battle scene renders as the widescreen scene it is, instead of a blank white native-ratio screen: src/core/Game.lua's renderer has no drawWidescreen channel at all (that is Game2's, and the Gen 2 path still uses it untouched), so the Screen now also answers the engine's own Gen 1 wide-battle contract -- isWideBattleLayout/uiSize ask Renderer:setUISize for the scene's own 960x540 canvas so Screen:draw lands drawContent on it 1:1, wantsFillScale fills the window with that surface, sgbPalettes supplies the whole-surface trueColor zone (mirroring src/battle/WideBattle.zones) and letterboxWhite/holdsUIAnchors match the native wide battle -- with Renderer.MAX_UI_WIDTH/MAX_UI_HEIGHT widened once, additively and only on Gen 1, from the engine's 640x576 bound to the scene's own 960x540 (Game2 never calls setUISize, so Gen 2 never reads the value). The Gen 2 path reads none of those Gen 1-only members and is byte-for-byte unchanged. In v1.8.9 the Gen 1 scene fills the UI SURFACE it is actually drawing into, instead of fitting itself to the WINDOW: Screen:draw asked love.graphics.getDimensions() (which reports the window, not the render target) for the size to fit its 320x180 design field into, so on any window larger than the scene's own 960x540 canvas the field was drawn OVERSIZED into that canvas and the canvas' own bottom and right edges then sliced it -- the bottom message/menu band lost everything below its top border (the F box kept only a sliver of frame) and the E box additionally lost its right edge and frame, reported by the user, with a screenshot, as the F and E boxes being pushed out of screen. It now asks the surface: the live canvas first, then Renderer:uiSize(), with love.graphics.getDimensions() kept only as the no-canvas fallback (drawing straight to the window, e.g. a headless test). The design field therefore lands 1:1 on the 960x540 canvas, which puts the F/E band's bottom frame exactly on the canvas' bottom edge and E's right edge exactly on the canvas' right edge -- the round-sixty-nine rule -- and the engine, which owns the window, blits that whole surface as before. This mirrors src/battle/WideBattle.lua, which draws the engine's own wide composition in native surface pixels and never asks the window how big it is; the Gen 2 channel (Game2's drawWidescreen, handed the window size) is untouched. Gen 1 HP-bar fix (v1.9.0): the HUD readout now resolves a battler's maximum HP through mon.maxHp OR mon.stats.hp, whichever that generation keeps it in. Gen 2's src/battle/gen2/Mon.lua stamps mon.maxHp on every mon, so Gen 2 reads the same field as before and is unchanged; but Gen 1's src/pokemon/Stats.lua (Stats.ensure) recomputes mon.stats.hp and never writes .maxHp, so the readout was handing the bar a nil maximum. On Gen 1 the HudTiles HUD shim turns a nil max into a maximum of 1, so the fill (hp*48/1) clamped to a permanently FULL bar -- the reported "HP bar isn't lowering when a Pokemon takes damage". The same `mon.maxHp or mon.stats.hp` fallback the engine itself uses (e.g. src/battle/gen2/Battle.lua:1397) now drives the bar fill, the bar's own green/yellow/red palette and the numeric current/max readout. Display only -- no combat logic and no Gen 2 behaviour changed. In v1.9.1 the F and E boxes are drawn as the cart's own Gen 2 textbox, as geometry instead of font glyphs, so they look native on BOTH generations: the scene's bottom band used to go through Font.drawBox, whose border glyphs are $79-$7E of whichever font page the RUNNING generation loaded -- and the two generations do not agree on that art. Gold's frames sheet carries the clean GSC double-line box, while a Red/Blue/Yellow boot has no frames sheet at all and falls through to Red's own font_extra border, the ornate clover-cornered double line -- so on Gen 1 the scene read as a Gen 1 text box rather than the Gen 2 one it exists to be. The frame is now drawn edge-for-edge from the same measures the engine's own Font.drawBox produces with the default Gold frame tiles: the horizontal tile's 1px outer line, 1px paper gap and 2px inner line; the vertical tile's 1px/1px pair; the 3-step rounded corners; and the bottom corners' clean 1px step (the cart's bl/br tiles are not vertical mirrors of tl/tr). It is plain rectangles at design-pixel granularity, so no ROM-derived art is shipped, no font page is registered, nothing is global and the engine's own Font state is untouched -- every other text box in the game keeps its own generation's art. F and E are now ONE box with the menu window's left edge drawn over it as a divider, which is the cart's own shape (BattleState:drawBottom draws a full-width message box and then the menu window over its right end), instead of two separately framed boxes whose facing borders ran two pixels apart down the middle of the band with every corner of both frames sitting at the junction -- the most visible way the pair stopped looking native. Rectangles also free the frame from tile alignment, so the band's fractional 6.5-tile height is simply 52px and the old math.ceil tile-rounding is gone. A layout preset that moves one pane away from the other still gets two separate frames rather than a divider drawn in mid-air. The custom action-menu button is now labelled FORMS (settings.lua's customButtonLabel) and the mod's player-facing strings say FORM. E label scales are unchanged: a 12-tile pane cannot fit native-size 2x2/cross text. In v1.9.2 the target picker is read off the field and the readouts sit exactly over their mons, both user-reported. (1) The F box's target picker no longer lists the candidates: it carries only its "Choose a target:" prompt, and the cursor is an arrow drawn on the field over whichever candidate is selected (Screen:drawTargetMark) -- five stacked one-pixel rectangles forming a downward triangle, positioned at that battler's own readout centre just above its box, with a one-pixel bob. Both up/left and down/right cycle it, since the candidates are laid out horizontally. (2) The eight-column sprite grid's pitch was only ~40.5px -- narrower than the 56.4px readout -- so spreadBoxCentres had to widen the readout row to keep the boxes off one another, and the row's outer boxes then stopped standing over their own mons, worst in a five-mon horde where the GUI spread too wide and broke its match with the sprite positions. The pitch is now the readout's own (COL_W = HUD_W + 2 = 58.4px), so each column is exactly one non-overlapping readout apart: the enemy team anchors at e6 = 276.8px and fills leftward (a horde fills e2..e6, centres 43.5/101.5/160.5/218.5/276.5), the ally team anchors at a1 = 35px and fills rightward, a boss takes e5 = 218.4px and a horde's lone ally a2 = 93.4px. The ally anchor absorbs the old +50px ALLY_X_SHIFT, so the lead ally does not move; spreadBoxCentres is now normally the identity (each readout comes back bit-for-bit on its own slot centre), kept only as the safety net for an over-full row. In v1.9.3 a 0-PP move is no longer delisted from the player's move menu: the list is built from Combat.allMoves (every move the battler still knows) with each entry carrying a usable flag, while the AI keeps usableMoves' PP filter; choosing a depleted move refuses with the native "No PP left for this move!" message and returns to the list at the same cursor, and a slot is only skipped entirely when no move has PP left (the stated no-Struggle gap) -- matching the native move menus. In v2.0.0 the action menu gains SWITCH (1.9.3 -> 2.0.0, a minor change that carries a 9 left; the mod semver is single-digit carry-left), a POSITIONAL trade of places between ADJACENT allies -- not the PKMN button's recall-and-replace switch. It is a LAYOUT capability, decided once per battle in Screen.new from the roster the preset actually shipped: the button exists only when two or more allies are alive on the field AND the battle is not a bossFight, so doubles and triples get it, singles and hordes do not, and a bossFight never does however many allies it fields. It sits second in the menu order -- directly UNDER FIGHT in every layout: the wide grid gains a middle row (FIGHT/PKMN, SWITCH/BAG, RUN) and the cross gains its empty middle-left cell (FIGHT/-/PKMN, SWITCH/FORMS/-, BAG/-/RUN), with column 1 widened 20 -> 24px to fit SWITCH and the centre budget 34 -> 30px to pay for it so the three-column block still measures 78px with a 2px margin either side; the list layout uses the cross's own 0.5 scale on a 7px pitch for its sixth row. Choosing it opens a swapSelect phase -- the F box reads Switch with whom? and the candidates are the owner's ADJACENT living allies -- navigated with up/left and down/right, A to confirm, B to back out to the action menu. A FILLED arrow (the same five-rectangle triangle the target picker draws) sits over the candidate under the cursor, and a HOLLOW frame arrow of exactly the same size is left over the OWNER's sprite -- the acting battler while choosing, and any queued owner until its swap resolves -- so the field always shows who owns each swap. The swap queues as kind=swap and resolves FIRST, before both move resolution and the PKMN switch queue, exchanging the two roster entries so the new positions hold for the rest of the turn and anything that reads positions (a spread move's centre, move-animation anchors) sees the new shape; B on the next slot's menu undoes a queued swap and drops its owner cue with it. The enemy side gets the same swap through two new exports: mod.exports.swapPositions(target, side, slotA, slotB) trades the places of two ADJACENT living battlers on either side (validated: adjacent indices only, both present and alive, battle not over) and mod.exports.swapCandidates(target, side, slot) reports which of a slot's neighbours can legally be traded with, so an enemy AI can reposition mid-turn with the field updating on the next frame. In v2.1.0 the FORMS (CUSTOM) button's activation is matched to the Pokemon whose action menu it was picked from, and the pick is announced so peer mods can follow it. battle_forms reads battle.player for every decision it makes -- each mechanic's eligibility when the list is built (formapi.gimmicks), its arm() hook when the pick is confirmed (a move-substituting mechanic like Dynamax rewrites that battler's moves there) and its real activate() at battle.turn_started -- while this scene pins battle.player to the FIRST player battler for the engine's own reads; so before this, on a doubles/triples layout a FORM picked from any other mon's menu armed and activated slot 1 instead of the mon that chose it. Every battle_forms call the FORMS bridge makes now runs with battle.player focused on the acting mon and restores the pin the instant it returns (pcall'd, so a raising call can never leave the field pointed at the wrong mon), and every step is announced: the scene emits its own FORMS_EVENT (mod.g9-Battle-Scene.forms -- a separate id from the existing CUSTOM_BUTTON_EVENT) carrying { phase, mon, species, slot, id, label, reason, battle, game, world } -- 'armed' when a pick is confirmed (naming the mon), 'used' when battle.turn_started actually consumed it, and 'cancelled' with a reason ('backed-out' on B, 'replaced' when a second pick supersedes the first, 'arm-refused' when battle_forms refuses the arm, 'activation-refused' when the armed id survives the turn-start) -- so a peer that reads battle.player later, and cannot assume it names the FORM's owner because the focus is transient, learns from the announcement which Pokemon used it and whether it was cancelled. The on-screen line names the mon too ('CHARMANDER armed MEGA EVOLVE!'). Annotation only in the engine's direction: the scene still owns no combat rules. In v2.1.1 a thrown ball plays the cart's OWN ball animation instead of resolving the instant A is pressed: the scene starts Gen 2's real ANIM_THROW_POKE_BALL through the same AnimRunner/BattleAnimView engine its move animations already use, with the ball drawn in the ball's own battle-object palette (Poke Ball red, Great Ball blue, Ultra Ball yellow, Master Ball green, ...; an unknown ball falls back to the grey default) and the throw re-aimed from vanilla's fixed single-battle spot onto the REAL acting Pokemon and the REAL target sprite on this mod's widescreen field (each axis scaled by real-gap / vanilla-gap, so vanilla's calibrated flight covers the real distance). The native catch plays out first: the ball shakes through the engine's own GetPokeBallWobble probability table (the cart's Poke/Great/Ultra Ball rates, with the 4th-shake guaranteed catch), the target is sucked in and its sprite hidden by the animation's own BATTLE_BG_EFFECT_HIDE_MON (the sprite pass honours that flag and removes the mon's sprite and anchor while it is held, restoring them on a breakout), and only when the animation genuinely ends does the scene report the answer ('Gotcha! X was caught!' or 'X broke free!'), so the outcome lands on the same beat the cart lands it (a caught ball's anim_keepsprites leaves the resting ball behind). Stock Gen 1 has no AnimRunner/BattleAnimView arm, so there the ball still resolves on the spot as before. Separately, cancel in the bag now returns to the battle's action menu on both generations: on Gen 2 the native Gen2PackMenu's own onClose pops the pack (and the scene swallows that same frame's B so the menu underneath cannot read it), and on Gen 1 B goes through the ListMenu's onCancel while A on the CANCEL row now also closes the list and returns to the action menu. In v2.1.2 the Gen 1 gap is closed: a Gen 1 boot HAS its own native battle-animation engine -- src/battle/AnimPlayer.lua, the subanimation player its own BattleState drives (src/battle/BattleState.lua:1399-1405) -- so whenever the Gen 2 AnimRunner/BattleAnimView pair is absent the scene now drives THAT, on exactly the contract the cart drives it on: a move's own battle_anims row, or the ball chain via BattleState:ballChain's toss -> POOF -> HIDEPIC -> SHAKE rows (opts {shakes, ball, ballFlicker} and all, with a captured ball's finalSprites left resting in OAM through the caught text). Its OAM sprites are remapped out of vanilla 160x144 space the same way the Gen 2 objects are -- the actor's real anchor and the real actor-target gap drive a per-axis scale -- and are grouped into connected components by OAM adjacency first, so a multi-tile composite (a 16x16 ball is four tiles) stays rigid under a non-unit scale instead of being pried apart. A row's move-sound byte routes through BattleState:playAnimSound's rule (GROWL/ROAR play the attacker's cry) and a toss's SFX_BALL_POOF/Tink play as their rows start. So a stock Red/Blue/Yellow boot now gets the game's own move animations AND the game's own thrown-ball catch animation (with the real shake count off Catching.attempt) instead of an instant resolution. A Gen 1 boot that also carries the Gen 2 assets still uses the Gen 2 arm, and Gold/Silver is byte-for-byte unchanged.
